topics.description:
The dot-com bubble had burst, and the Nasdaq had fallen more than 50% from its peak. Yet the sense of deflation ran deeper than the numbers. Since Jobs and Wozniak had founded Apple, the personal computer had been at the heart of the digital revolution. By 2001, experts predicted that this central role was coming to an end—it had become mundane.
It was then that Jobs conceived a new strategy: the personal computer would transform into a digital hub, coordinating a variety of devices—from music players to video recorders and cameras. If the personal computer became a hub, mobile devices could be simpler, lighter, and more specialized, relying on the computer for coordination.
topics.mainCitation: The mark of an innovative company is not just creating ideas, but also knowing when to leap forward upon realizing it has fallen behind.

topics.description: In 2000, people were saving music on their computers, ripping it from CDs, or downloading it from file-sharing services like Napster and burning it onto blank CDs. In other words, many people were creating their own CDs, but Apple wasn’t meeting this demand. Jobs noticed that the music-burning software of the time was complicated and difficult to use. It was then that Bill Kincaid appeared, later adapting MP3 functionality for Macs through the program SoundJam. The final Apple product became known as iTunes.
topics.mainCitation: Join the music revolution with iTunes and make your music devices even more valuable.

topics.description:
The next step was to create a portable music player. Complex tasks could be handled on the computer, while simpler ones could be done on the device. This is how the iPod was born.
Jobs’ main requirement was: “Simplify!” If you wanted a song or a function, you had to reach it in just three clicks.The iPod wouldn’t have a power button—a feature that later became standard on most Apple devices.
topics.mainCitation: The iPod became the essence of everything Apple was meant to be: “poetry connected to engineering, arts, and creativity, intersecting with technology and bold yet simple design”
